shadow_trades.reasoning_summary: Trading away my only A to get a second B would leave me with 0 A, 2 B, 1 C, reducing variety and utility since I'd have none of a good instead of an even spread. Current equal distribution (1,1,1) is preferable.

Trading 1B for 1A would just swap equal quantities, resulting in 2A/0B/1C, moving from balanced to unbalanced inventory which decreases variety value. I prefer to keep my balanced 1/1/1 bundle unless a trade adds net variety value.
Trading away my only B for 2 more A would leave me with 0 B, hurting variety; my current balanced bundle is worth more than the proposed skewed one.
Trading away my only C to get a second B would make my bundle less diverse (1,2,0), reducing utility given my preference for variety. I'd rather keep balanced holdings.

Trading away my only B to get a 2nd C would leave me with 1A,0B,2C, reducing variety and utility since I'd have zero of a good. Equal 1-1-1 holdings are already balanced; this trade unbalances my inventory without net benefit.
Trading away my only B for more C would leave me with 0 B and 3 C, reducing variety which I value. Current balanced holdings (1,1,1) are preferable.

Trading away my only A for a second B would leave me with 0 A, 2 B, 1 C, reducing variety and making my bundle less balanced. Since I value variety, this trade decreases my utility rather than increasing it.
This trade would give me 2A, 0B, 1C, creating imbalance since I'd lose all B. I prefer maintaining variety across all three goods, so trading away my only B for a second A reduces my utility.
Giving up my only B would leave me with zero variety in that good, while ending up with 3 A is excessive. I'd rather negotiate a more balanced trade, like 1A for 1B or similar.

I currently have equal amounts of A, B, and C (1 each). Trading away C for B would just shift the imbalance (2 B, 0 C) without improving diversity - it would actually reduce variety since I'd go from a balanced 1-1-1 to an unbalanced 2-1-0 split.

I currently have equal amounts of A, B, and C (1 each). Trading away B for C would just shift the imbalance from C to B, giving me 2 C and 0 B, which doesn't improve variety - it just moves the deficit around.
Trading away my only B for more C would leave me with zero B, reducing variety which I value. Current balanced inventory (1,1,1) is already good; I'd rather seek a trade that keeps some balance.
I currently have 0×B, 2×A, 2×C. Trading 1×A for 1×B gives me a more balanced bundle (1,1,2), increasing variety value since B was my scarcest good.
Giving up both my A would leave me with none, hurting variety; I'd rather trade 1 A for 1 B to balance my inventory evenly across A, B, and C.
Trading 1C for 1B moves me from (2,0,2) to (2,1,1), increasing variety balance across A,B,C which improves my utility given I value diversity.

Giving up both of my C would leave me with none, trading variety for variety but overall decreasing my diversified holdings too much. I'd prefer a smaller trade, like 1B for 1C, to maintain balance across all three goods.
I currently have 0×B and 3×A, so giving up one A (my most abundant good) for a B (which I lack entirely) increases variety and overall utility.
Trading 2 excess A for 1 B gives me a more balanced bundle (A1,B1,C1), which better satisfies my preference for variety despite giving up more units of A.

I currently have 0 B and 1 C; trading away my only C for a B gives me better variety (1 A... wait, 3 A, 0 B, 1 C -> 3 A, 1 B, 0 C), which balances my holdings better across types and B is becoming scarce/valuable.
I currently have 0 B, 2 A, 2 C. Trading 1 A for 1 B gives me a more balanced bundle (1A,1B,2C), increasing variety value since B was my scarcest good.
Giving up both A units leaves me with none, hurting variety. I'd prefer a 1-for-1 trade instead of 2A for 1B.
I currently have 0 B and 2 C, so trading 1 C for 1 B improves variety balance (2,1,1 vs 2,0,2), increasing overall utility under diminishing marginal value for repeated goods.
Giving up both C units would leave me with none of that good, hurting variety. I'd prefer a smaller trade like 1C for 1B.
Giving up my only B to get A would leave me with zero B, which hurts variety and B is noted as increasingly valuable/scarce. Not an improvement.
Trading 1 B (which I only have one of) for 2 A improves diversity and total holdings, since A is currently zero and highly valued due to scarcity in my inventory.
I have 0 A, 1 B, 2 C. Trading 1C for 1B gives me 2B, 1C, 0A - more balanced inventory and B is becoming scarce/valuable, improving my variety-based utility.

I have 0 A, 1 B, 2 C. Giving away my only B to get a third C would leave me with 0 B, which hurts variety badly, especially since B is reportedly in high demand. I'd rather keep my B and seek A instead.
Giving up all my C to end up with 0×A, 2×B, 0×C reduces variety too much; I'd rather keep some C and seek A instead.

I currently have 0 A, 1 B, 2 C. Giving up my only B for more C (going to 4 C) would leave me with 0 A, 0 B, 4 C - heavily skewed and losing my only unit of B, which the market says is valuable. This reduces variety and utility; I'd rather keep B or trade for A instead.

I currently have 2 A, 0 B, 2 C. Trading 1 A for 1 B balances my inventory to 1 A, 1 B, 2 C, increasing variety value since B goes from 0 (very valuable) to 1, while A only drops from 2 to 1, still fine. This improves overall utility given diminishing marginal value on duplicates.
Giving 2A for 1B would leave me with 0 A, destroying variety - too steep a price. I'd prefer a 1A for 1B trade instead.

Currently I have 0 B and 2 C, so gaining a B (filling a zero-quantity slot) while losing a C (reducing from 2 to 1) increases variety and overall utility under my diminishing-returns preference for variety.

Giving up 2C for only 1B would leave me with zero C and only 1B, reducing variety and overall utility compared to my current balanced A2/C2 holdings with B0. The trade is unequal in quantity and doesn't improve my diminishing-returns utility.
